statusDefinitions.reference: Uses the v72 authored shell and active release contracts.
statusDefinitions.browser-computed: The visible result is computed locally from the current input in browser code.
statusDefinitions.limited-browser: A bounded or heuristic browser implementation is available; stronger claims require external validation.
statusDefinitions.export-only: The platform generates a reproducible external workflow but does not claim to execute it in the browser.
statusDefinitions.legacy-migration: Retained from the last fully green integration baseline and scheduled for migration to the v72 shell.
statusDefinitions.unavailable: Not presented as a computed capability.
statusDefinitions.derived-browser: Computed from an already completed finite browser result without launching a separate estimator; interpretation remains conditional on that result.

limitations: The Model Studio currently owns deterministic ODE projects; stochastic, agent, population-genetic, evolutionary and data-driven models retain dedicated builders.
Two-parameter sweeps vary independent rectangular ranges with all other parameters nominal and are not Sobol, Morris or uncertainty analyses.
Three-dimensional and color-encoded plots visualize computed finite trajectories or grids; they do not certify chaos, causality, global stability or identifiability.
Browser explicit integration remains exploratory for stiff or high-cost systems and must be independently verified with an appropriate external solver.
SBML events, rules, packages, non-unit compartments and unsupported MathML are rejected rather than partially imported; CellML, SED-ML and COMBINE/OMEX are recognized but not executed.
Requested tolerances constrain the numerical solve; they do not quantify model-form, parameter, measurement or biological uncertainty.
Changing a scientific or numerical input marks existing evidence stale; stale plots are visible as prior evidence but result/image exports are disabled until rerun.
Initial conditions, parameter values and ranges, time span, output density, method, step controls, rtol, atol and safety are user-editable and validated before computation.
Browser methods are intended for moderate explicit systems.
The local Jacobian timescale ratio and rejection evidence are stiffness heuristics, not a stiffness certificate.

Verify against SciPy is an optional independent numerical comparison; first use requires network access unless a local Pyodide distribution is configured, and agreement does not validate the model or data.
The Model Report Card records computation and declared limits; it is not a scientific-validity certificate.
Publication-grade results require independent convergence and domain validation.
The foko.model-ir/1 reaction-network route is a limited local schema, not SBML, CellML, Modelica or a DAE/hybrid-system standard.
Reaction rates and direct equations still use the platform restricted expression evaluator and must be independently checked.
The fatty-acid and FADNS browser examples are reduced public research models, not the complete calibrated repositories; they require independent reproduction before publication use.
The SBML browser route supports a strict reaction subset only; it rejects unsupported semantics and requires the user to review time-span and numerical experiment settings.
A converged local root does not establish global root completeness.
Deterministic multi-start samples a finite set of initial guesses and is not exhaustive.
Parameter scans reuse nearby roots but are not pseudo-arclength continuation and cannot confirm folds or Hopf bifurcations.
Dynamical stability is reported only for a declared dx/dt=f interpretation and only for 1x1 or 2x2 Jacobians in the browser core.
Finite-difference Jacobians and local Newton solves require independent validation for publication or safety-critical use.

The full four-state fatty-acid branch workflow does not certify physical bistability or complete root sets; converged roots that violate declared constraints are excluded from physical interpretation.
The conditional MalCoA–FA slice has an exact local 2×2 spectrum, but it is not the stability of the full four-state model.
The FADNS occupancy example is algebraic at fixed substrate pools, so dynamical stability is not applicable.
The direct browser algorithm assumes time-homogeneous propensities and non-negative integer states.
Finite ensembles provide Monte Carlo estimates, not exact probability laws or parameter confidence intervals.
Trajectories reaching the configured event cap are censored and are never presented as complete runs.
Pointwise empirical quantile bands do not provide simultaneous coverage.
Mean-field overlays are curated deterministic approximations and need not equal the finite-population ensemble mean.
Tau-leaping, SDE integration, time-dependent hazards, and large-scale ensembles require an external workflow.
The browser reports evaluated candidates, not certified local or global optima.
Inequality and equality constraints are searched through a quadratic penalty and checked independently against a user-declared feasibility tolerance.
Differential evolution, random search, and multi-start are seeded finite-budget heuristics; repeated runs do not prove global optimality.
Finite-difference projected descent can fail on nonsmooth, poorly scaled, or ill-conditioned problems.
The Pareto view is a seeded finite candidate sample, not an exact frontier.
KKT conditions, convexity, uniqueness, sensitivity, and robustness require independent analysis.

The 15 application examples are analytic surrogates and do not execute CFD, quantum hardware, clinical image registration, finite elements, molecular dynamics, Maxwell solvers, power-flow solvers, game engines or control-plant simulations.
Distance-to-reference is available only when a preset declares a known analytic reference vector; arbitrary user objectives have no assumed true optimum.
The engine is a constant-size, non-overlapping, two-deme Wright–Fisher teaching model at one biallelic locus.
The elementary two-deme FST ratio is not a Weir–Cockerham estimator or historical-demography inference.
No VCF/PLINK ingestion, linkage, recombination, coalescent inference, ancestry, GWAS, relatedness or genomic quality-control pipeline is implemented in this lab.
Inference remains conditional on sampling, measurement quality, model assumptions, multiplicity decisions, and the analysis plan.
Mean imputation is exposed only as a sensitivity tool and understates uncertainty.
Classical OLS intervals and tests assume an appropriate linear error model and independent observations.
ANOVA is omnibus; no post-hoc pairwise procedure is computed in the v72.4 browser reference.
ROC AUC and average precision are empirical on the supplied sample and do not establish calibration, utility, or transportability.
Kaplan-Meier and log-rank output do not provide a hazard ratio or causal treatment effect.
Browser output does not establish causality or external validity.
The curated examples are synthetic teaching and stress-test datasets; they do not represent empirical evidence or benchmark external validity.
PCA is a standardized covariance decomposition with finite-sample eigensolver evidence; components are not latent mechanisms or causal factors.
Nonlinear least squares is a local numerical search; convergence does not establish a global optimum or unique parameter vector.
Local covariance intervals and bands rely on a linearization of the fitted model and an appropriate residual error model.
Inverse-variance weighting treats the supplied sigma values as known, strictly positive observation standard deviations.
Pairs bootstrap resamples rows as exchangeable units and is not valid for clustered, serially dependent or hierarchical observations without redesign.
Profile SSE scans, local correlation matrices and the practical-identifiability verdict are finite local diagnostics; they do not certify structural identifiability or global uniqueness.
Experimental-design advice is a local covariance-based sensitivity heuristic over a finite candidate grid; it does not guarantee identifiability or an optimal experiment.
In-sample R-squared, AIC, residual plots and influence measures do not establish out-of-sample validity or mechanistic truth.
The browser reference is intended for small dense matrices and uses floating-point arithmetic.
Singular values are estimated from eigenvalues of A-transpose A; very small singular values are sensitive to squaring the condition number.
Rank and nullity depend on the selected numerical tolerance and matrix scaling.
The browser eigensolver accepts real symmetric matrices only; general nonsymmetric spectra require an external library.
A small residual does not imply a well-conditioned or scientifically correct system.
PCA is centered but not standardized and remains sensitive to scale and outliers.
A stationary Markov candidate does not certify uniqueness, irreducibility or mixing time.
The browser reference is intended for small graphs and deterministic layouts.
Weights must be declared as additive costs or connection strengths; operations do not silently reinterpret both meanings as equivalent.
PageRank, closeness and betweenness encode different notions of importance and need not agree.
Label propagation is a deterministic heuristic in this implementation and does not identify a unique latent community partition.
The node-removal curve uses descending initial degree without adaptive re-ranking and is not a calibrated failure model.
Graph metrics do not establish causality, mechanism or measurement validity.
Nested and repeated cross-validation reduce optimistic selection bias but do not create external validity; small samples can still produce highly variable estimates.
Cross-validation estimates internal performance for the supplied sample and does not establish external validity or robustness to distribution shift.
Binary classification requires explicit 0/1 targets; labels are never silently recoded.
Standardization is fitted inside each training fold to reduce preprocessing leakage.
Mean imputation is restricted to selected features as a transparent sensitivity option; missing targets are dropped.
Permutation importance is predictive and conditional on feature correlation, redundancy and the fitted model; it is not causal importance.
K-means and PCA are exploratory Euclidean summaries and do not identify natural groups or latent mechanisms.
Large boosted ensembles, deep learning, nested tuning, GPU training and production deployment require external workflows.
PCA shown beside supervised or clustering results is computed from the same prepared feature matrix and remains descriptive rather than predictive validation.
A browser diagnostic is not evidence that a neural PDE model was trained.
Only plots compatible with the current computed result are offered; export-only workflows expose the reference trajectory rather than fabricated training evidence.
Sparse equations are conditional on derivative estimation, sampling, noise, scaling, candidate terms, threshold and regularization and are not automatic mechanistic truth.
Browser inverse and surrogate adapters are bounded teaching diagnostics and do not establish identifiability, uniqueness, calibration or replacement validity.
Publication-grade SciML requires independent external training, held-out validation, convergence studies and domain-specific checks.
One-state results cannot select two- or three-dimensional phase views or trajectory PCA; incompatible plots are removed rather than rendered as errors.
Nonzero synthetic noise is generated from an explicit seed and exported with the configuration; changing the seed changes the sampled perturbation while preserving the deterministic base trajectory.
The browser grammar requires explicit multiplication and supports arithmetic, powers, parentheses and the elementary functions sin, cos, tan, exp, log and sqrt.
The simplifier applies a small transparent rule set and deliberately avoids domain-changing cancellation such as x/x = 1.
One-dimensional roots are detected over a finite interval by sampled near-zero values and sign-change bisection; repeated tangent roots can be missed.
Small-system equilibria are candidates found from a deterministic finite start set and are not an exhaustive exact solve.
Jacobian stability is local numerical evidence and does not establish global dynamics, uniqueness or bifurcation structure.
General integration, exact equation solving, factorization, complex branch analysis, special functions and general ODE solving require the SymPy export or another external CAS.
Exact-count mode requires non-negative integer state counts summing exactly to N². Fraction mode uses deterministic largest-remainder allocation and reports the exact counts actually simulated.
Custom Agent models are restricted to validated declarative local transition rules (spontaneous, neighbour-contact and neighbour-threshold). Arbitrary JavaScript is not executed.

One algorithmic step is one configured lattice sweep. Random-with-replacement gives one update attempt per site on average; shuffled sweep visits every site once. Neither is automatically biological, social, epidemiological or physical time.

Finite-ensemble quantiles and Monte Carlo standard errors describe simulation variability under fixed rules and parameters; they do not quantify parameter uncertainty, measurement error or model discrepancy.

Cluster counts, largest-cluster fractions, spatial agreement and entropy are descriptive lattice diagnostics whose interpretation depends on state coding, occupancy, topology, initialization and boundary conditions.
Finite-horizon terminal labels and absorption times are conditional on the configured grid, horizon, update schedule and seed. They are not stationary-distribution or asymptotic certificates.
The curated T-cell, cell-cycle, fatty-acid, SIR, voter, segregation, predator-prey and forest-fire examples are qualitative mechanisms or stress tests rather than calibrated empirical models.
Continuous-space, network-agent, adaptive, reinforcement-learning and large-scale agent simulations require external workflows.
Worker cancellation terminates the active ensemble and publishes no partial result. A main-thread fallback is used only when Web Workers are unavailable and is explicitly disclosed.
When Plotly cannot mount, the interface renders the same computed result through a built-in canvas fallback and labels the rendering path.
The fatty-acid particle presets are research-inspired lattice abstractions, not the published semi-mechanistic FADNS ODE and not quantitative kinetic models.
Dynamic lattice snapshots come from the representative derived seed; ensemble bands and endpoint distributions summarize independent runs and must not be conflated.
State legends are placed below categorical lattice panels to preserve the data region.

During computation, both visible Agent panels are driven by paced incremental numerical states from the same representative seeded realization. The pacing delay changes only display timing, not the seeded result; stored-frame replay is manual and non-looping.
The Workbench is an orchestration and comparison route; it intentionally exposes a smaller configuration surface than each focused lab.
Every adapter returns one computed result with compatible plots, diagnostics and provenance. It does not create decorative outputs or a second copy of the numerical engines.
Configuration URLs do not preserve prior computation evidence. Shared configurations must be recomputed.
Advanced model authoring, large datasets and production-scale runs remain in focused or external workflows.
The Bayesian example is a one-rate conjugate model, not a general posterior sampler or hierarchical modeling system.
Design evidence is local to a two-parameter exponential model; standards checks do not certify SBML, SED-ML or COMBINE archives.
Continuation uses canonical analytic normal forms rather than pseudo-arclength continuation of arbitrary residuals.
PDE and SDE examples are bounded references, not general FEM/SPDE/stiff stochastic solvers.
Genomic examples use synthetic independent biallelic loci and do not ingest VCF/PLINK files or infer demography, linkage or selection.
Study sweeps run locally on one closed-form model and are not a distributed workflow engine.
All results are conditional on the selected output, initial conditions, time window, parameter ranges, perturbation or sample count, solver and tolerances.
Local finite differences are local and step-dependent; discontinuities, event thresholds and poor scaling can invalidate derivative interpretations.
Initial conditions affect trajectories but are not treated as sensitivity factors in this release.
Morris is a screening method. Its sigma combines interaction and nonlinearity and does not identify either mechanism separately.
Jansen first/total and Saltelli second-order estimates assume independent uniform input ranges. Raw finite-sample estimates and intervals are intentionally not clipped.
The Fisher-information view is a local range-scaled trajectory approximation under a constant independent noise scale; normalized column alignment is not posterior parameter correlation.
The browser refuses projected workloads above its guarded state, parameter, ODE-solve, pair-count, or state-time envelope. Larger studies must use the exported Python/SALib workflow.
No adjoint, sensitivity-equation, eFAST, Shapley, correlated-input, symbolic-identifiability, profile-likelihood, certified continuation or PDE/PINN sensitivity engine is present.
State and parameter Jacobians are local right-hand-side derivatives along the nominal trajectory; they are not propagated sensitivities or stability certificates.
OFAT and tornado plots hold all nonselected parameters nominal and therefore omit interactions.
Directional profiles depend on the declared parameter-range normalization and chosen direction.
Two-parameter response surfaces fix all remaining parameters nominal and are not variance decompositions.
Time-resolved Jansen estimates reuse the finite seeded global design; low-variance time points may be unresolved.
Histogram mutual information and RBF-HSIC are bounded-sample permutation screening diagnostics, not variance fractions or causal measures.
The normalized Morris trajectory view displays only a bounded subset of the computed designs when many trajectories are requested; all trajectories still contribute to the statistics.
State-resolved first and total indices apply the selected scalar metric to each state using the same finite seeded Jansen design; they are not independent replications.
The optional two-parameter response surface is available in Local and Global variance modes but remains an OFAT-style bounded grid with all other parameters fixed at nominal values.
A finite state grid can miss roots that are not bracketed or approached closely.
Stability is one-dimensional and local; candidate events are not certified bifurcation points.
Pseudo-arclength continuation, Hopf points, periodic orbits, multidimensional branches and codimension-two analysis require external specialist software.
Landscapes are fixed, haploid, asexual and frequency independent.
There is no recombination, diploidy, spatial structure, migration, changing environment or evolutionary-history inference.
A finite seeded realization does not establish mutation-selection equilibrium or inevitable convergence to the global optimum.
The Gaussian-process interval is conditional on the RBF kernel and user-selected hyperparameters.
The random-feature surrogate is not deep-network training and reports no predictive uncertainty.
All displayed errors are in-sample; deployment requires held-out validation and domain assessment.
The workspace is limited to browser-scale one-input regression.

platformHardening.plot_compatibility: dimension- and result-gated selectors with distinct visible panels
platformHardening.rendering_status: computed status follows successful Plotly or canvas rendering
platformHardening.scope: browser-scale reference diagnostics; external validation remains required
platformHardening.canvas_mode: collapsible input and diagnostic rails for a wider scientific canvas
platformHardening.central_workspace_breakpoints: two readable simultaneous plots or one Focus plot; public 3-up controls removed
platformHardening.agent_execution: Web Worker ensembles with cancellation, progress and stale-result rejection
platformHardening.sciml_reproducibility: explicit deterministic noise seed and exported provenance
platformHardening.reliability_first_workspace: two simultaneous computed plots or one focused plot; visible 3-up controls removed
platformHardening.model_input_contract: every active scientific lab exposes editable input and/or a local import route
platformHardening.browser_test_install: only Playwright is installed through npm; Plotly, math.js and KaTeX remain vendored
platformHardening.agent_spatial_evidence: representative temporal snapshots plus ensemble agreement, diversity and occupancy summaries
platformHardening.example_atlas: searchable provenance-classified catalog with 251 curated routes
platformHardening.model_ir: validated foko.model-ir/1 direct ODE and reaction-network lowering
platformHardening.external_architecture_review: mxlweb-core concepts reviewed; no source or binary redistribution

modelInputRoutes.optimization: editable variables, bounds, objectives and constraints; configuration JSON import
modelInputRoutes.population_genetics: editable demography, initial allele frequencies, selection, dominance, mutation, migration, ensemble size and seed
modelInputRoutes.advanced_methods: editable bounded reference parameters for Bayesian, design, standards, continuation, PDE, SDE, genomic-summary and study-sweep modules
modelInputRoutes.bifurcation: editable scalar right-hand side, constants, parameter/state domains, finite scan resolution and inspection slice
modelInputRoutes.evolution_landscape: editable landscape family or complete genotype-fitness table plus population, selection, mutation and seed
modelInputRoutes.ai_modeling: editable local x,y data and transparent Gaussian-process or seeded random-feature surrogate settings
modelInputRoutes.statistics: local tabular data upload and editable table
modelInputRoutes.fitting: local tabular data upload and editable data
modelInputRoutes.linear_algebra: editable matrix/vector; text, CSV or JSON import
modelInputRoutes.networks: editable edge list; text, CSV or JSON import
modelInputRoutes.ml: local data upload and ML configuration JSON import
modelInputRoutes.sciml: local trajectory/model text upload plus editable workflow configuration
modelInputRoutes.agent: exact initial state counts or fractions, 20 curated presets, dynamic spatial evidence, declarative custom model JSON and configuration import
modelInputRoutes.symbolic: editable expressions and scope; text or JSON import

modelAtlas.boundary: A named domain example is not automatically calibrated or externally validated.

limitations: The registry can only expose metadata declared by the lab preset or page selector.
It prevents incompatible presentation but does not independently validate the scientific meaning of every plot.
A single compatible plot is shown in Focus mode rather than duplicated.

analysisTaxonomy.policy: Only capabilities backed by current computed data appear in runtime plot menus; export-only and unavailable methods remain explicit reference entries.
